A Person-Centered and Compassionate Approach to Coaching Neurodivergent Teens & Adults.

Virtual & In-Person Options Available

Real-Life Executive Function Coaching

A Person-Centered and Compassionate Approach to Executive Function Coaching.

Virtual & In-Person Options Available

What is Real-Life ADHD Coaching?

ADHD (or executive Function coaching) helps clients who are experiencing challenges often related to ADHD. Our coaches work with clients to improve organization, time management, task initiation/completion, attentional control, self monitoring, and more. Services can often lead to better self-regulation and advocacy in school, work, and life.At Life Skills Advocate, we prioritize client emotional well-being.Because here's the thing...Executive function (or dysfunction) has a ripple effect on quality of life. We call this the EF Ripple Effect. The Ripple Effect is the emotional impact that clients experience as a result of their struggles. Our coaches are trained in recognizing these impacts and in coaching clients with informed and evidence-based approaches.

"I've never met a provider who understood my daughter so well..."

Ruby - parent

"I've never met a provider who understood my daughter so well, let alone on the first day. The way you communicated with her never put her on the defensive and she was able to open up without hesitation. Everything on your list are things we've been trying to work on with her for so long and yet, I think she'll be able to hear you. I'm so grateful to you and hopeful for the possibilities."

Who Do We Work With?

While a formal diagnosis is not a prerequisite to receiving coaching support from us, some of our clients have a diagnosis of autism, ADHD, NVLD, OCD, intellectual disability, anxiety, and others. While we recognize diagnosis as a factor, our focus is on the whole person.

*case by case

Clients who may benefit from our support often need assistance with multiple topics including, but not limited to, organization, planning, time blindness, flexibility, problem-solving, attentional hyperactivity, working memory, decision-making, analysis paralysis, and procrastination. Clients may also wish to discuss demand resistance/avoidance, sustaining friendships, building confidence, transitioning to the next phase in their life, acquiring new skills, and advocating for themselves.

While not all of our clients are ADHD, many are. We are trained and educated in addressing neurodivergences that causes Executive Functioning challenges!

At any age, ADHD can be challenging to navigate. We provide research-based assistance anyone age 14 and up who want to develop strategies to address their ADHD.

High school can be a difficult time developmentally and can be very overstimulating.

College and vocations create a lot of transition and often benefit from structure, which can be hard with ADHD functioning!

All stages of adulthood require executive functioning skills and also can include seasons of transition, which can exacerbate executive dysfunction. In a culture that isn't always accommodating for neurodivergence like ADHD, clients often develop shame and stress.

As coaches, we want to help clients stop living under that pressure, and to collaborate with them in  implementing strategies that bring relief and stronger executive functioning!

"...flexible and creative while also ensuring a disciplined approach to progress."

Kristin - parent

"We had been looking for a coach for our son for nearly a year when we found Chris. He was able to connect with our teenage son in the middle of COVID and quickly established a rapport with him in a short amount of time. As the pandemic continued, Chris became an important support figure who brought needed structure and also some levity and fun. He is flexible and creative while also ensuring a disciplined approach to progress. We appreciate that Chris is available in between sessions for Zach to connect, when needed, and adapting weekly focus areas based on where he is on that day/week."

When you book a free

you get to meet with one of our coaches and talk through what you need!

Life Skills Advocate is a judgment free environment where our coaches personally understand the impact of being neurodivergent. We believe in a shame-free approach with curiosity and a growth mindset. Our favorite metric for success is the comfort level our clients have with their own brains - whether their brains are ADHD, ASD, OCD, or any other neurodivergent experience. We don’t believe in coaching our clients to be neurotypical, rather we want to advocate for their abilities to thrive as they are!

Why A Person-Centered Approach?

Why A Person-Centered Approach?

Because it works.

Aside from the common sense that people are more likely to accept help from people who get them and who they have a personal connection with, empirical studies (Thomas, 2006) of outcome research cite "The Big Four" common factors for change.

The Big Four:

  1. Relationship Factors (30%)
  2. Hope & Expectations (15%)
  3. Models & Techniques (15%)
  4. Extra-therapeutic Factors (40%)

Estimated Percentages of the Common Factors of Change

Relationship Factors

The alliance between the coach and the client. Including the coach's warmth, empathy, encouragement and acceptance of the client.

Hope & Expectations

The client feeling hopeful and believing in the credibility of process.

Models & Techniques

The coaching models, strategies & tactics used to move clients towards action to improve their situation.

External Factors

The elements the client brings with them into coaching. Including strengths, circumstances, support system, environment, and chance events.

marilyn - parent

"I was so happy when we found out about Life Skills Advocate. My son is Asperger and has struggled with organizing his life and executive skills, even now at 32. With Chris's help, they are figuring out plans to help him be a more responsible person and figure out what is important to him and how to make this happen. We enjoy the newsletters, templates and of course the one-on-one attention. Chris is a very approachable person and knows what he is talking about. Easy to work with as a parent and 'gets' his clients. He has even helped out with my son's manager at work to make that environment run smoothly. One-on-one in this climate is wonderful. Chris has been great at making these sessions comfortable for us, and responds quickly to questions and problems."

Coaching Session Framework

Each coaching session is uniquely tailored to the individual client. We strive to make sure our clients have time to process their progress and setbacks, to collaborate with their coach on strategies and goal, and to practice what they are learning with their coach.

We also offer accountability check ins throughout the week depending on what the client needs!

What is Real-Life ADHD Coaching?

Real-Life ADHD Coaching (otherwise known as executive function coaching) helps individuals improve their mental processes such as organization, time management, task initiation, attentional control, self-monitoring and others across real-life contexts such as school, work and daily life.

With coaching and compassionate accountability in tandem, clients can expect to achieve not only better performance in these areas, but also a better relationship with themselves and others.

At Life Skills Advocate, we also prioritize our clients' emotional regulation as it pertains to executive functioning and understand the emotional ripple effect it can have on overall quality of life.

Our coaches are trained to recognize the emotional impacts of executive dysfunction and use informed and evidence-based approaches to help clients overcome their struggles.

Who can benefit from Real-Life ADHD Coaching?

Real-Life ADHD Coaching is available to anyone whose executive functioning skills (e.g. organization, planning, time management, flexibility, problem-solving, attentional control, etc.) are impacting their performance at school, work, and life in general.

Many of our clients struggle with real-life challenges such as making & sustaining friendships, building confidence, transitioning to the next phase in their life, acquiring new skills, and advocating for themselves. Our coaching services can support these areas and more.

How does the coaching process work?

Once coaching is determined to be a mutually good fit at the discovery meeting, we will pair you with a coach that aligns with your learning style, schedule and other preferences.

During the first meeting with your coach, you will get to know each other and outline goals and put together a working roadmap.

From there, each session within the coaching process is tailored to the individual client and their needs. Clients will have time to reflect on their progress and setbacks, work with their coach to develop strategies, and practice what they have learned with their coach's guidance.

In addition, we offer accountability check-ins throughout the week to ensure clients are staying on track and making progress in their desired areas.

What is Real-Life ADHD Coaching?

ADHD (or executive Function coaching) helps clients who are experiencing challenges often related to ADHD. Our coaches work with clients to improve organization, time management, task initiation/completion, attentional control, self monitoring, and more. Services can often lead to better self-regulation and advocacy in school, work, and life.

At Life Skills Advocate, we prioritize client emotional well-being.

Because here's the thing...

Executive function (or dysfunction) has a ripple effect on quality of life. We call this the EF Ripple Effect. The Ripple Effect is the emotional impact that clients experience as a result of their struggles. Our coaches are trained in recognizing these impacts and in coaching clients with informed and evidence-based approaches.

Who Do We Work With?

While a formal diagnosis is not a prerequisite to receiving coaching support from us, some of our clients have a diagnosis of autism, ADHD, NVLD, OCD, intellectual disability, anxiety, and others. While we recognize diagnosis as a factor, our focus is on the whole person.

*case by case

Clients who may benefit from our support often need assistance with multiple topics including, but not limited to, organization, planning, time blindness, flexibility, problem-solving, attentional hyperactivity, working memory, decision-making, analysis paralysis, and procrastination. Clients may also wish to discuss demand resistance/avoidance, sustaining friendships, building confidence, transitioning to the next phase in their life, acquiring new skills, and advocating for themselves.

While not all of our clients are ADHD, many are. We are trained and educated in addressing neurodivergences that causes Executive Functioning challenges!

Why A Person-Centered Approach?

Why A Person-Centered Approach?

Because it works.


Aside from the common sense that people are more likely to accept help from people who get them and who they have a personal connection with, empirical studies (Thomas, 2006) of outcome research cite "The Big Four" common factors for change.


The Big Four:

  1. Relationship Factors (30%)
  2. Hope & Expectations (15%)
  3. Models & Techniques (15%)
  4. Extra-therapeutic Factors (40%)

Estimated Percentages of the Common Factors of Change

Relationship Factors
30%

The alliance between the coach and the client. Including the coach's warmth, empathy, encouragement and acceptance of the client.

Hope & Expectations

The coaching models, strategies & tactics used to move clients towards action to improve their situation.

External Factors
40%

What is Real-Life ADHD Coaching?

Real-Life ADHD Coaching (otherwise known as executive function coaching) helps individuals improve their mental processes such as organization, time management, task initiation, attentional control, self-monitoring and others across real-life contexts such as school, work and daily life.

With coaching and compassionate accountability in tandem, clients can expect to achieve not only better performance in these areas, but also a better relationship with themselves and others.

At Life Skills Advocate, we also prioritize our clients' emotional regulation as it pertains to executive functioning and understand the emotional ripple effect it can have on overall quality of life.

Our coaches are trained to recognize the emotional impacts of executive dysfunction and use informed and evidence-based approaches to help clients overcome their struggles.

Who can benefit from Real-Life ADHD Coaching?

Real-Life ADHD Coaching is available to anyone whose executive functioning skills (e.g. organization, planning, time management, flexibility, problem-solving, attentional control, etc.) are impacting their performance at school, work, and life in general.

Many of our clients struggle with real-life challenges such as making & sustaining friendships, building confidence, transitioning to the next phase in their life, acquiring new skills, and advocating for themselves. Our coaching services can support these areas and more.

How does the coaching process work?

Once coaching is determined to be a mutually good fit at the discovery meeting, we will pair you with a coach that aligns with your learning style, schedule and other preferences.

During the first meeting with your coach, you will get to know each other and outline goals and put together a working roadmap.

From there, each session within the coaching process is tailored to the individual client and their needs. Clients will have time to reflect on their progress and setbacks, work with their coach to develop strategies, and practice what they have learned with their coach's guidance.

In addition, we offer accountability check-ins throughout the week to ensure clients are staying on track and making progress in their desired areas.
